- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if price spiked 3+ days ago, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overshoots in early periods (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at +5% above 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model fails to adjust; force a 1–2% upward correction in next forecast.
